open.thesis: 84% rostered nationally and dropped by Footballers - an ownership anomaly, not a bad player. Listed WR1 for Jacksonville ahead of Meyers. PHRASING CORRECTED 14 Sep 16:40, twice now: jaguars.com publishes three FIRST-STRING receivers by alignment - Parker Washington slot, Brian Thomas Jr. left with Travis Hunter second, Jakobi Meyers right. It is not a WR1/WR2/WR3 ranking, and a summarised read of that page renders it as one, which is how this run first mis-stated it before the 13:30Z review caught it. Nobody has passed Thomas; they hold different jobs. Week 1: 3 catches for 40 in a game Jacksonville led 24-0 at half with Lawrence attempting 23 passes. He left with a shoulder and returned in the second quarter - second shoulder scare of his year, no imaging and no team statement published.
open.falsifiedIf: Target share stays under about 18% through week 3; or a Jaguars statement puts the shoulder in doubt; or Meyers out-targets him in week 2. The depth-chart clause is retained but must be read as 'loses his first-string alignment', not 'is listed second'.
open.review: Week 1 re-reviewed 14 Sep 13:30Z, UNRESOLVED and the previous review partly CORRECTED. This morning's earlier entry said Jacksonville's official depth chart lists Parker Washington 'in the top receiver slot', which overstates it. The chart read directly from jaguars.com lists three first-string receivers by alignment: Parker Washington first-string SLOT, Brian Thomas Jr. first-string LEFT with Travis Hunter second behind him, and Jakobi Meyers first-string RIGHT. Washington has not passed Thomas; they hold different jobs. The falsification condition is about Meyers or Washington passing him on the depth chart and that has not happened. Thomas's 3 of 3 for 40 is still thin and Lawrence attempted only 23 passes in a 34-3 blowout. Condition left as written, reviewed again after week 3. No action. RE-REVIEWED 14 Sep 22:43Z, UNRESOLVED. The alignment-versus-ranking distinction has now caused a mis-statement in two consecutive runs. Flagged here so the next run reads the chart itself rather than a summary of it.

open.thesis: Pittsburgh's listed RB1 and the primary passing-down back. Chem switched to full PPR, which doubles the value of the receiving edge that had made him a sit. Reviewed 14 Sep: HELD. Week 1 was 15 touches for 73 yards in a 20-13 win and Yahoo reported him taking the early lead in the Pittsburgh backfield. Warren 10.3, Tuten 9.8. No snap-share or goal-line split was retrievable, so the hold rests on touch count and one beat report rather than on usage data.
open.falsifiedIf: Dowdle out-touches him materially two weeks running, or Warren's target share drops below Dowdle's.
open.review: Week 1 reviewed 14 Sep, HELD on the evidence the thesis named. Pittsburgh's week 1 depth chart lists Warren as RB1 and Rico Dowdle as RB2, and Kenny Gainwell — who led the Steelers with 73 receptions in 2025 — is now in Tampa Bay, which is the vacated passing-down work the thesis was built on. Warren turned 15 touches into 73 yards for 10.3 against a 12.6 projection, so the role is right and the output was ordinary. Neither falsification condition tripped: Dowdle did not out-touch him and did not out-target him. Review again after week 3. No action.

open.thesis: Reconstructed after the fact from reporting. Likely signed 3yr/$40M to follow Harbaugh from Baltimore and is the undisputed Giants TE1 and primary slot option, with Nabers coming off an ACL and a receiver room only four deep.
open.falsifiedIf: Nabers returns to full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%, or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.
open.review: Week 1 reviewed 14 Sep, HELD emphatically. Likely went 8 of 8 for 78 and two touchdowns for 27.8 against a 9.5 projection. The falsification condition turns on Nabers reaching full health and Likely's route share falling under about 60%; Nabers is still managing the knee and was reported as willing to discuss a snap-count arrangement to play at all, so the condition is not close to tripping. Review after week 4.

open.thesis: 8 of 9 for 138 and two scores, led Carolina in every receiving category while McMillan was quiet until garbage time. 50% rostered is an anomaly in a ten-team league. Chem priority resets weekly so the claim is free. AMENDED 14 Sep 16:40, risk raised: Coker was photographed in a walking boot Monday with an ankle tweak and ESPN has flipped him to QUESTIONABLE in the league file. He told reporters he expects to play; NBC, Yahoo and DraftKings Network all carry the same line. Carolina's first week 2 practice report lands Wednesday, AFTER the claim processes at 07:00Z. Claiming blind is accepted because Chem priority resets weekly. Sequencing: the JuiceJam trade must be sent before 07:00Z Wednesday or this claim deletes Stafford out of the offer; if the trade lands first, this claim needs no drop.
open.falsifiedIf: Coker is limited or DNP in Carolina's Wednesday practice report, or carries a designation into Sunday; or McMillan reasserts as the clear alpha and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across weeks 2-3.
open.review: Re-researched 14 Sep 13:00Z, HELD and strengthened. Independent reporting confirms Coker led Carolina in snaps (57) and routes run (40) ahead of McMillan's 56 and 39, and adds that McMillan's slot rate was 21.4% against 19.8% last season — the same role rather than an expanding one — while describing Coker's 11 and 12 personnel work as secure for the season. Claim still pending, clears 2026-09-16T07:00Z. One correction carried into today's card: yesterday asserted no trade exists in Chem where both sides gain. An exhaustive one-for-one and two-for-one pass on season projections found seven, several involving Stafford, so the drop is not as free as yesterday claimed.

open.thesis: Start Likely over Pitts from week 2. This overrides ESPN's own season projection, which prefers Pitts 181.4 to 156.2 and ranks him TE7 to Likely's TE12. The override is on role: Likely is a full-time tight end for the first time on a three-year $40M deal with Nabers still managing a knee, and went 8 of 8 for 78 with two scores. Amended 14 Sep: it is NOT true that Pitts lost his role. He ran a route on 81% of Atlanta's dropbacks, tied 7th among week 1 tight ends, on one target that was an underthrown deep ball. The reason he scored nothing is the quarterback — Tua Tagovailoa ruled out Thursday with an oblique, Penix inactive and not at 100%, Cooper Rush 12 of 22 for 144. This is a close call between two intact roles, not a rout. AMENDED 14 Sep 16:40, confidence reduced again. Two things landed today. Atlanta still have no week 2 starter: Stefanski said Monday he has no updates on Tua's oblique or on Penix and no timeline, and Rapoport put Penix at 'next week or week 3'; Rush was 12/22 for 143 with 2 INTs in a 20-13 loss. That favours Likely. Against it: the Giants draw the Rams in week 2, a top-three week 2 streaming defence, while Pitts gets Carolina at home - on matchup alone the call flips. Held because who is under centre outranks matchup quality in the research order. Trigger is Atlanta's Wednesday practice report.
open.falsifiedIf: Tua Tagovailoa returns and Pitts clears five targets in week 2; or Pitts out-scores Likely in two of the next three weeks; or Nabers reaches full health and Likely's route share drops below about 60%; or Theo Johnson takes the 11-personnel snaps back.
open.review: Reviewed 14 Sep 13:30Z, UNRESOLVED and materially weakened by reporting that was not read yesterday (Pitts at 81% route participation). Call held rather than reversed, because reversing a lineup card eight hours after publishing it on a coin flip is the churn STRATEGY section 3 exists to prevent. First real evidence arrives in week 2.

open.thesis: Consolidation two-for-one with JuiceJam (team 10). Their starting quarterback is Jared Goff at 277.8, the second-weakest starter in the league, and Stafford projects 303.4 and is the man this week's Coker claim drops for nothing. McLaurin is the sell: Washington signed Stefon Diggs in August into a room already holding Deebo Samuel and Zach Ertz, Diggs went 4/55/1 in his debut while McLaurin returned 3.4 on a 12.3 projection, and McLaurin is 30 coming off a quad injury that ended a four-year run of 17-game seasons. DeVonta Smith is their slot-4 starter and this asks for a starter — it is survivable for them only because DJ Moore sits at slot 20 on 209.0 and backfills. Computed +21.8 me / +3.8 them on season projections. Also corrects yesterday's claim that no mutually profitable trade exists in this league. RE-VERIFIED 14 Sep 16:40 against a fresh 22:16Z snapshot, not carried: recomputes to exactly +21.8 me / +3.8 them on season projections (2070.3->2092.1 and 1966.4->1970.2). On weekly projections it is -0.9 for them, so it clears on the season horizon only - the reverse of the usual one-week warning, and the likeliest reason it gets declined. Smith's role confirmed by reporting: Philadelphia's undisputed WR1 with A.J. Brown in New England, three scoreless catches in week 1. NOTE: the 22:09Z run published Chem with an empty trades array, which removed this proposal from the app while it was still live. Restored this run. URGENCY: must be sent before 07:00Z Wednesday.
open.falsifiedIf: They decline, or the Coker claim processes Wednesday 07:00Z and removes Stafford from the offer, whichever comes first. Also falsified if Diggs's target share collapses after week 3 and McLaurin's role recovers, which would make selling him at his lowest point the mistake.

Declined anyway: Pineiro was dropped FOR Boswell on 8 September, six days ago, and reversing a kicker slot inside a week is the exact pattern the log already carries twice as CHURN. closed.summary: One bench slot went Goedert -> Allgeier -> Likely in five days. Each step was defensible on projection; the sequence gained nothing and cost two roster moves.
Recommended dropping Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker on 13 Sep. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4; Tucker's Bowers-vacuum thesis now has a return date on it. Not acted on.

A 13 Sep run recommended adding Xavier Worthy and dropping Isaiah Likely, on the reasoning that a second TE is structurally unplayable in a RB/WR flex. Likely then scored 27.8 with two touchdowns. The structural argument was sound and the conclusion was still wrong, because it valued the slot rather than the player.

Adding Isaiah Likely on 13 Sep resolved RIGHT - 27.8 with two touchdowns. Note for the pattern file: the add landed at 19:03Z, two hours after Pitts's 17:00Z kickoff, so he could never have been started in week 1. The cost of a Sunday-evening add is a whole week, not a lineup slot.
